ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Connect $OD$. Since point $B$ is symmetric to point $A(-3,0)$ with respect to the line $x=-1$, the coordinates of point $B$ are $(1,0)$. According to the problem, the coordinates of point $D$ are $(m, -\frac{4}{3}m^{2}-\frac{8}{3}m+4)$. Therefore, the area $S_{\text{quadrilateral }ABCD}$ equals $S_{\triangle OAD}+S_{\triangle OCD}+S_{\triangle OBC}$, that is, $\frac{1}{2}\times 3\times\left(-\frac{4}{3}m^{2}-\frac{8}{3}m+4\right)+\frac{1}{2}\times 4\times(-m)+\frac{1}{2}\times 1\times 4=-2m^{2}-6m+8=-2\left(m+\frac{3}{2}\right)^{2}+\frac{25}{2}$. Since $-2<0$, when $m=-\frac{3}{2}$, the maximum area of quadrilateral $ABCD$ is $\boxed{\frac{25}{2}}$. At this point, the coordinates of point $D$ are $\boxed{\left(-\frac{3}{2}, 5\right)}$.
